rationale: Three-lens review complete (blind, edge-case, acceptance). Acceptance lens confirms all 6 spec criteria pass with test/lint/build evidence. Edge-case lens found zero unhandled paths. Blind lens raised 4 concerns; 3 were investigated and refuted against the live repo (no other SkillActions/SkillDetailsActions callers exist per grep + clean tsc --noEmit; no e2e/playwright/cypress directory or any remaining reference to the old skill-name-/skill-details-name- literals exists anywhere in the repo; all touched entity id fields are already typed string, not number). One finding survives: the SkillCard/SkillActions useId() pair — the only one of the 6 pairs migrated in this task — has zero test coverage proving the same generated id is threaded to both the Card heading and SkillActions' NavigationMore contextId, which is exactly the drift this task exists to prevent.

business_review.criterion: No aria-labelledby reference depends on an id template written in a different file
business_review.evidence: All 6 named pairs now import a shared builder from src/utils/ariaIds.ts or use useId() co-location; repo-wide grep confirms no remaining cross-file literal duplication among the 6 pairs.

business_review.criterion: Each of the 6 pairs resolved via useId() co-location or an imported builder from src/utils/ariaIds.ts
business_review.evidence: 4 builder pairs (DataSource, Provider, MCPServer, Workflow) and 2 useId() pairs (SkillActions/SkillCard, SkillDetailsActions/SkillDetails) all implemented per the spec's per-pair table; ariaIds.ts exports exactly the 4 spec'd functions with unchanged template strings, verified by src/utils/__tests__/ariaIds.test.ts.

business_review.criterion: The 4 hardcoded-id tests converted to DOM resolution
business_review.evidence: SkillDetailsActions, DataSourceActions, ProviderActions, and WorkflowsList accessibility tests all now resolve aria-labelledby off the rendered DOM instead of asserting a literal string. ProjectSettingActionsCell correctly left untouched.

business_review.criterion: Full test suite, lint, and build green
business_review.evidence: Full vitest run: 4745 passed, 1 pre-existing skip. npm run lint: clean. tsc --noEmit: clean. npm run build: succeeds.

business_review.evidence: New 'Cross-component ARIA id sharing' section added with the 3-case decision rule; constants-usage.md has a 'See also' cross-reference.

business_review.criterion: Implementation risk: duplicate DOM id in workflow pair verified and guarded
business_review.evidence: WorkflowsList.tsx hoists nameId to one variable per row gating both the nameId prop and navigationSlot together, preserving mutual exclusivity with WorkflowCard's navigationSlot ?? WorkflowActions fallback. New WorkflowCard.duplicateId.test.tsx asserts exactly one element carries the id on both render paths.

standards_review.notes: All 8 commits in the diff match 'EPMCDME-8420: Capital sentence.'

findings.problem: SkillCard.tsx generates titleId via useId() and threads it to both Card's titleId prop and SkillActions' new nameId prop, but no test verifies these two usages receive the same value. SkillCard.test.tsx (15 tests) has zero references to titleId, nameId, contextId, or aria-labelledby.
findings.impact: This is the only one of the 6 migrated pairs with no direct test evidence that the id-sharing link holds. A future refactor that accidentally calls useId() twice (once inline in each prop) or drops the shared variable would silently break the accessible name — the exact drift-on-rename failure mode this task exists to eliminate — with no test catching it.
findings.recommendation: Add an accessibility test for SkillCard (or extend SkillCard.test.tsx) that renders SkillCard, resolves aria-labelledby off the NavigationMore-produced button, and asserts it points at the same id as Card's heading element — following the DOM-resolution pattern already used in MCPServerActions.accessibility.test.tsx and WorkflowCard.duplicateId.test.tsx.
